newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan listed firms' 1st-half nets shrink 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan listed firms' 1st-half nets shrink 11 pct.

text.p: Total net profits of listed Taiwan firms fell 11 percent in January-June from the first half of 1995 due to political tensions with China and a slow economy, a local report said on Monday.
Net profits for Taiwan's 364 listed firms totalled T$127.7 billion in the first half of 1996, the Commercial Times said.

The report attributed the overall decline to Beijing's sabre rattling in the Taiwan strait in the months before the island's historic direct presidential election on March 23 and a slowdown in Taiwan's "Asia dragon" economy.
The report said China's war games and missile tests had caused severe capital outflows and hurt many domestic-oriented industries, such as construction, on Taiwan.
The government statistics bureau said in August that GDP growth for the entire year would reach only 5.89 percent, well below a 6.17 percent forecast issued three months earlier.
Firms in the financial and insurance sector reported the highest total net profits during the six-month period at T$38.7 billion, followed by the information and electronic sector's T$34.1 billion.
Petrochemicals and plastics' profits were T$12.3 billion.
